q: Children below fourteen are found mixing chemicals in a fireworks unit, the employer pleading poverty and parental consent. Which statement is correct?
options: The employment is unlawful, consent being immaterial, and rehabilitation follows
The employment is lawful where the parents of the child have consented in writing
The employment is lawful outside school hours in a family enterprise
The employment is unlawful only if the unit is registered as a factory
expl: Hazardous employment below fourteen is barred and consent cannot validate it.
why: The third option states a genuine statutory exception and applies it to a hazardous occupation, where it does not operate.
trapnote: A real exception applied to the wrong category. The family-enterprise exception excludes hazardous work.

q: A State imposes admission and fee rules on a minority institution that leave it no effective choice in selection. Which statement is correct?
options: All regulation of a minority institution is impermissible once the right is established
All regulation is permissible, the right being subject to any law made by the State
Regulation is permissible only where the institution receives aid from the State
Regulation for standards is permissible, but rules destroying the minority character are not
expl: Reasonable regulation for excellence is permitted; destruction of character is not.
why: The second and third options represent the two extremes, and the answer lies between them.
trapnote: Regulation yes, destruction no. Both extremes are wrong in this area.

q: A State legislature enacts a law prescribing punishment for compelling payment of a religious tax and restricting the rights of its own police force. Which statement is correct?
options: Both provisions are valid, public order and police being State subjects
The first provision fails and the second is valid as a matter of police administration
Both provisions fail, each subject being within Parliament's exclusive competence
The second provision fails and the first is valid as a matter of State taxation
expl: Both subjects are reserved exclusively to Parliament by the rights chapter.
why: The second option reasons from the ordinary distribution of powers, which is displaced here.
trapnote: Two separate exclusive powers, both in Parliament. The general distribution does not govern.

q: Consider a trust-established institution now administered by the State which continues religious instruction. Which statement is correct?
options: The instruction must cease, all State-administered institutions being barred
The instruction may continue, the institution falling within a narrow express exception
The instruction may continue only with the consent of each guardian
The instruction must cease unless the trust is re-executed to omit the requirement
expl: The exception operates where the institution was established under a trust requiring such instruction.
why: The third option applies the consent rule from a different situation in the same provision.
trapnote: This is the one situation where instruction continues without consent. It is narrow and express.

q: Women are held at a roadside establishment against thumb-marked loan papers and are paid below the minimum wage. Which statement is correct?
options: Forced labour is made out on the wage ground, and trafficking provisions may also apply
Forced labour requires proof of physical confinement, which is absent here
The arrangement is a civil debt matter with no constitutional dimension
Forced labour is made out only where the workers concerned are citizens of India
expl: Sub-minimum wage is itself forced labour and the protection extends to all persons.
why: The second option states the field assumption the leading decision was delivered to displace.
trapnote: Wages and debt are the trigger. Confinement need not be proved.

q: Consider: 1-A fee charged for facilities provided to pilgrims is permissible. 2-A levy for the upkeep of one religion is barred. 3-A levy on all persons for the upkeep of all religions is permissible. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: A levy for the promotion of religion is barred whether it favours one or many.
why: The third statement is attractive because even-handedness usually cures discrimination, but the bar is on the purpose.
trapnote: The bar turns on the purpose, not on even-handedness between religions.

q: A mob prevents members of a community from entering a public temple, and an officer is directed to ensure entry. Which statement is correct?
options: The direction is unlawful, entry being a matter of religious custom alone
The direction is lawful only during a festival notified by the State government
The direction is lawful, the State being empowered to throw open such institutions
The direction is unlawful unless the temple receives aid from public funds
expl: The power to throw open public religious institutions of a public character is express.
why: The fourth option imports a funding condition that belongs to a different provision altogether.
trapnote: The power is express and does not depend on funding. Funding conditions belong elsewhere.

q: Consider: 1-An aided institution may deny admission on grounds of religion. 2-A minority institution has leeway in selecting students. 3-Both propositions rest on the same provision. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
None of them
expl: Only the minority-leeway statement holds; aided denial on religion fails and the provisions differ.
why: The first statement is barred by the admission-equality provision, and the two provisions are distinct.
trapnote: Two provisions, two rules. Leeway in selection is not a licence to deny on prohibited grounds.

q: A child of thirteen years and eleven months works one day in a mine with protective equipment and double wages. Which statement is correct?
options: The employment is barred; the test turns on age and hazard and admits no de minimis exception
The employment is permissible, adequate safety measures having been provided
The employment is permissible for a single day, the prohibition being on regular employment
The employment is barred only if the wages paid are below the statutory minimum
expl: Age and hazard are the tests; duration, safety and wages are immaterial.
why: Each wrong option introduces a mitigating factor that the provision does not recognise.
trapnote: No mitigating factor cures it. Age plus hazard is the whole test.

q: A bonded child from a minority community is refused admission to an aided school on religious grounds and is trafficked for labour. Which combination is correct?
options: Only the trafficking provisions apply, admission being a matter of institutional discretion
Only the admission-equality provision applies, bonded labour being a statutory matter alone
Neither applies, the school being a private body outside the rights chapter
Forced labour and trafficking provisions apply, and the refusal breaches admission-equality
expl: Three distinct provisions are engaged on these facts.
why: Synthesis items punish the selection of a single provision where several operate together.
trapnote: Several provisions can operate on one fact-pattern. Do not stop at the first.
